_step150: the shot leaves on a tap's release (planning step 137): each tap goes down on `tick` and comes up on `release`, the next tick unless it says later
_about: 1-22, authored for wave 4a (round 1) on the build with the portal tap, reflector, knights, stone and wake rules. Two breakable
walls (x 300 and 332) shut the way to the door and only a rolling stone breaks one; the two stones sit on a platform (x 70 to
234, top y 82) that the player, on the floor below it, cannot reach. So he is put on it. A portal over the platform's right
end at (232, 60) (tap 40, placed 82; from the floor the ray must clear the single block's top-right corner, and every x from
226 to 238 at y 50 to 70 does) and one on the player (tap 86, 4 after the landing): he comes out on the block (88). He walks
left (92-258) behind stone 727, which he pushes into stone 753, along the platform; 753 leaves its left end at about tick 225
and 727 after it, both land on the ramp and roll down (he takes two crystals on the way, 172 and 112). 753 breaks the first
wall on 308 and rolls on, undamped, to the second wall, which it breaks on 434. That tick is the route's one loose number: it
moved between 400 and 446 under a 1-tick change of any earlier input (the held-friction creep of R3-2, the stones' roll has no
damping in this port), and 508 under a 3-tick one, so the last two taps wait for it with 24 ticks to spare. He walks back right
(264-304) to stand at x 214.8 on the block (the window is x 200 to 230, the hold's end good for 298 to 310, and 311 walks him
off the block's right end), and
when the second wall is gone shoots a portal into the door room at (417, 190) (tap 458, placed 526; over the door, the ray
passes under the blocks at y 98 and over both stones) and one on himself (tap 532): he comes out over the door and falls into
it. Won on tick 535. Four portals, two of five crystals: medal 2 (the golden score is 2 portals and all five crystals; the
pair that carries the player is the extra pair). No achievement. Leans on: the player's push of two stones along a platform
(about 0.3 u a tick, ticks 90 to 225: the port's solver), the stones' undamped roll (R3-2) and the portal pair's one use.
AND ON A RULE THE ORIGINAL MAY NOT HAVE: wall 1 breaks at stone hit 3.11, wall 2 at hit 0.088, a stone creeping up to it. The
port breaks a wall on touch (R3b-2), where the decoded callback (ETHBeginContactCallback_breakable_wall #16-33) needs a stone
faster than scale(1.5), and its stones pass no momentum on (no restitution step, G10-14); so wall 2 is probably meant, in the
original, for the second stone 727 arriving fast (here 727 comes to rest at the ramp's foot, unused; inferred, not measured).
Build that gate and this route must be re-flown (wall 2 would need a fast stone).
